newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar rallies on renewed fund buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar rallies on renewed fund buying.

text.p: White sugar futures powered higher as a renewed bout of fund buying pushed the nearby August contract over $330 a tonne in solid early volume, traders said on Tuesday.
Fund buyers moved into the spot position towards the end of Monday's session, driving it up nearly $4 higher to reach $328.00.
Market sources said fund players had been attracted by August's good liquidity and strong technical picture.
"They came in late yesterday on the strength of New York and they've continued again this morning. The rest of the board is getting dragged up on the back of it," said one trader.
"Most of the volume is tradeable volume and I would say the majority of it is the funds on the buy side."
But the recent strength has also pushed August into overbought territory, with the 14-day RSI (reltaive strength indicator) standing at 82 and above the 70-value overbought buffer.
"One has to beware a correction but for now it is best to go with the flow," said Darren Gurner, a technical analyst at Sucden. Next resistance points were placed at $333.50, followed by $341.00.
At 1145 GMT August was up $2.90 at $330.70, an intraday high, and October was up $2.30 at $320.80. Overall volume amounted to 1,308 lots, the vast majority of which was in August.
A sprinkling of crosses was also noted, including some trade crosses and commission house interest in December/March.
Trading in Paris was also dominated by August, which was up $2.90 at $329.50. October was untraded and Matif volume totalled 383 lots.
